text_fidelity_a:
Basily 25 Oz Infuser Water Bottle With Carry Around Strap I've tried a few other styles of infuser and have fallen love with the review sample of this one that I recently received. To be honest I love the other models that I have used too. Some are more complicated than others, but all have proven to be effective and efficient at infusing waters.

Here are the main reasons why I prefer this one. First, it's reasonably light compared to two other brands that I own. This is made of a light weight plastic that is BPA-free, and seems resilient to dropping (which I managed to do.) One of my other ones is glass, which is both heavy and fragile, and the other plastic one I own is heavier and lacks the carrying strap.

A second reason why I love this is the infusing basket is simple, deep and easy to remove. It does not have the juicing section that other infusers have, but since I usually infuse with lime or lemon quarters and eighths, it does not need one. More importantly, the basket has a bail that makes it easy to remove. Plus there are no complicated o-rings or seals and this one has never leaked.

Still another reason is the cap has a positive locking mechanism that keeps it sealed when you are not drinking from it. And the 'icing on the cake' is the drinking spout is large, but not so large that my fruits come out. Of course, you will probably have to adjust the way you cut fruits or vegetables if you are accustomed to finer pieces because the spout it not tiny.

Bottom line: this is a no-frills infuser that may lack some of the features of other brands, but it's also less complex. I love the fact that it's grab and go. Plus the large infuser seems to do a better job of marrying flavors with your water. If you want a real treat try Acqua Panna Natural Spring Water as the base for your infused drinks.
text_fidelity_b: Basily 25 Oz Infuser Water Bottle With Carry Around Strap

text_fidelity_a: Fitbit Charge 3 Fitness Activity Tracker I loved this product... at first.  The app is great.  I loved getting notifications.  So much information.  I really felt motivated to hit my goals and stay active, well-hydrated and well-rested.  Unfortunately, I now fall into the category of people who have a Fitbit lemon.  The notifications were the first to go.  I tried everything under the sun to get the notifications back.  That includes practically doing the rain-dance based on the threads on their support site.  Calling customer service - forget it!  I have a full-time job!  I can't sit on hold for 20 minutes.  I gave up and figured I still had a great product without the notifications.  Then just this week it ran out of battery and I cannot bring it back to life.  The support threads are so laughable.  It tells you if all else fails to try resetting by hitting the button in the pinhole on the underside of the watch.  But it also says not to use a paperclip or pointed object.  What else should I use?  I tried a paperclip anyway and it doesn't fit.  So now I have a $150 product that doesn't work at all and is past the timeline to return to Amazon.  You may not get a lemon in which case you may love this watch.  But... you may be unfortunate like and get a watch that you loved for 4 months and are now out of $150.  Good luck!
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Charge 3 Fitness Activity Tracker

text_fidelity_a:
Schrade SCHF36 Frontier 10.4in Stainless Steel Full Tang Fixed Blade Knife with 5in Drop Point and TPE Handle for Outdoor Survival, Camping and Bushcraft I have zero business affiliation with amazon or Shrade. I just like to help people make a decision on purchasing affordable gear. Many times I have bought less expensive gear and was sorry I did. However this won’t be the case with Schrade. If you are just getting into camping/bushcraft start with this knife. I bought my knives directly from the Schrade website (shut down now) about 2-3 years ago. I have 3 of their knives Sch37, Sch57, and Schf52; and was only out of about $60 for all 3. They are great knives for a beginner. Yes, they have some issues. But they may not bother everyone.

The Bad: The basic handles are not the most comfortable over long periods of use. Later, get the micarta scales the basic scales are not comfortable when chopping or don’t chop.

The chimpping on top is a bit aggressive when not wearing gloves and doing percussive tasks.

The protective coating scratches and stains but; it can be removed and cleaned if you have the time. I like to keep my things looking brand new. I may remove the coating at some point.

The sheath is not the greatest but at least you don’t have to buy one.

The good: it comes with a sheath, a sharpening stone, and a fire steel. You don’t get that with $500 knives.

It can accomplish every task a $500 knife can.

You can sell the knife/knives for what you paid; if you want to upgrade.

You can keep them to loan out or for a buddy to use.

Best of all is the price. You get to test out your skills for less than $30 bucks with this knife.
text_fidelity_b: Schrade SCHF36 Frontier 10.4in Stainless Steel Full Tang Fixed Blade Knife with 5in Drop Point and TPE Handle for Outdoor Survival, Camping and Bushcraft

text_fidelity_a:
Mountain House Chicken & Dumplings with Vegetables This is just astonishingly easy to make and it tastes way better than expected. Usually dehydrated foods are flavorless and lifeless, but this chicken and dumpling concoction actually smells like chicken when you open the package and you can recognize the peas & carrots immediately. (see the photo)

I added the cup and a half of boiling water to the pouch per the directions, sealed the pouch and let it cook for 12 minutes. Opening the pouch releases a chickeny aroma and everything is sort of mushy and definitely cooked and ready to eat. The texture is fine - the chicken chunks are edible and not rubbery at all. The carrots & peas are fine as well. The only issue was with some of the dumplings - these are made of biscuits instead of noodle based and some of them were actually a bit crunchy. I'm not sure if this was deliberate or if maybe I should have used a little more water than the directions suggest. There's not real broth with the cup and a half - it's more like a bowl of porridge. The flavor is good and I didn't need to add any salt to this at all. I would consider adding a couple of these to our Hurricane Emergency supply kit for sure.
text_fidelity_b: Mountain House Chicken & Dumplings with Vegetables

Backyard Champs Disc Jam Flying Disc Game I first played can jam (aka Kan Jam) with DIY cans and Frisbees. I didn't even realize it was something people bought, and it sure was fun. This replicates that experience or rather it replicates the Kan Jam game. As with all variants, its easy to learn and makes for great backyard fun for parties and gatherings. Most folks have some level of Frisbee skills, and most folks have played a game with a goal/goalie. This piggy-backs off of that common knowledge.

While the game is fun, the parts in this kit are basic. This helps keep the cost down and keeps it highly portable. Both are sound choices, but it would feel better if the actual cost were a bit lower. I'm thinking $25-30 more than close to $40. Price aside, it doesn't take up that much space when storing, and it's looking plenty durable.

I'd definitely recommend checking out Kan Jam and related Frisbee games. They're fun! As far as the hardware, this is definitely something I can recommend, but I cannot see why this would be better than another competing product.

text_fidelity_a:
ALPS Mountaineering Meramac 4-Person Tent, Sage/Rust Having had, and liking, several ALPS Mountaineering products ([[ASIN:B004R7L7YU ALPS OutdoorZ Commander Backpack, 5250 Cubic Inches]] and [[ASIN:B006H1YL1U ALPS Mountaineering Stuff Sack]]), and being in the market for another tent, I chose the 4 Person tent knowing that (1) I'll never really need it to hold four people and (2), I will not be carrying this in my backpack. This tent was specifically bought for car camping.

I like that it has a carry case instead of stuff sack. I'm not quite certain why, but this just seems to make more sense to me. I'm probably less likely to forget the case. I'm also happy with the set up. Instead of sliding poles through a sleeve as several of my other tents do, this is simply a connect the poles, lay them out, put the ends into the stoppers and clip the tent to the poles. It's much easier going up and, if you were in a good location, you really wouldn't need to put in pegs and could freestand.

The one thing about this tent that I didn't like or understand is why they were put a pole under the fly and have you pull the fly up and over the erected tent like that. Honestly, I looked and looked at the instructions and did not see a single thing about that. YouTube came to the rescue in the form of "Mr. Tent".

Since I've not had the opportunity to actually test it out of yet - sure I could put it up in the livingroom and have "Camp InHouse", and I may yet do that, I'm going to leave this review as is and modify it in the future should the need arise. I do not anticipate any problems because I am familiar with the brand, style of tent and my expected usage.

text_fidelity_a:
ZOOOBELIVES Ultralight Backpacking 32-50F Down Sleeping Bag - 27oz Ultra Compact 650 Fill Power Envelope Sleeping Bag for Hiking, Camping and Backcountry, Lightweight and Compressible – Alplive T400 I received this sleeping bag 5/26/2022. Upon unpackaging, this sleeping bag smelled absolutely horrible! It had a very, very overpowering smell of poultry. No way could I sleep in this bag on a backpacking trip with this smell.
This mission statement on their storefront "ZOOOBELIVES is the brand of ZOBON INC of its own kind, which prides itself in selling unique outdoor products of the highest quality.", does not hold true with this sleeping bag.
For $84 I would expect that the down used in this bag, would be clean and free of smells. Especially the smell of nasty feathers.
I washed this bag in the washing machine, and put it in the dryer on low heat. About 20 minutes into the dry cycle, the smell of this bag had our laundry room smelling like a farmyard!
So I pulled the bag out, and hand washed it. I had to drain the water and refill the wash tub twice, because the water was so dirty. And the smell. I cannot even begin to tell you just how bad it smelled. A mixture between a wet dog and a chicken farm. It was bad! So bad, that our washroom smelled bad enough that I had to Febreeze it!
I let the bag soak in the wash tub both times for 30 minutes.
After the 2nd soaking/wash, I rinsed the bag and the water was finally clean.
I then placed the bag back in the dryer and threw 3 bounty sheets in with it to make sure that the smell was indeed gone.
After about 2 hours in the dryer, the sleeping bag was completely dry. And the horrible stench was gone.
IF this company truly prides themselves on "Highest Quality" gear, then the QC for the down in these bags needs to be a lot better!!
I purchased a down bag from one of the major manufacturers of tents, and that sleeping bag had NO bad smells. And I have also purchased multiple of the packable down throws, and none of them have smelled this way!
In the pictures, you can see just how dirty the water was. The final picture of the bag in the wash tub, was after the 2nd wash and during the rinse. The water was clean. And the smell was gone as well.
So I spent 3 or 4 hours cleaning a "New" sleeping bag!
Now that it is clean, the loft is even better than it was before I washed it! I will update on the performance of this bag when I get it out in the woods.
It was purchased as a summer bag, so it should perform good as that. But, we will see.
text_fidelity_b: ZOOOBELIVES Ultralight Backpacking 32-50F Down Sleeping Bag - 27oz Ultra Compact 650 Fill Power Envelope Sleeping Bag for Hiking, Camping and Backcountry, Lightweight and Compressible – Alplive T400

text_fidelity_a:
94 Piece First Aid Kit Packed with First Aid and Survival Essential by Sirius Survival A good first aid kit is a good thing to keep in the car when traveling and I selected this kit to keep in one of the vehicles because all of us are road warriors these days. Of course, the hope is that it is never needed, but when one is needed it's an invaluable resource. This is an interesting kit, and it has some pluses and minuses.

This is a small kit that fits nicely under a seat, in a seat pocket, or in a center console. Finding a place for it in a car or truck should be no issue at all.

There's a lot going on in this kit. It has a lot of the typical first aid items - bandages, gauze, cotton swabs, anticeptic wipes, and even a foil emergency blanket. There's some really odd things in here too - a flint, a compass, a whistle and a multi-tool are the stand-outs. This is not a typical first-aid kit but is also a basic survival kit.

The multi-tool is the standout in the whole kit and is worth the cost of the whole kit. It seems to be made fairly well, it is heavier than some of the cheaper ones I have seen and used and it has the basic tools you'd expect - pliers, a knife, screwdriver, etc. It includes a set of bits as well.

The compass is relatively cheap but it does work.

The remainder of the components in this kit are farily nondescript. All will work in an emergency capacity.

As a first aid kit this isn't so bad. However, this thing tries to be a survival kit as well, and on that basis there's an important omission - there's no flashlight in this kit. Even a small $5 flashlight would make this kit more complete and capable.

This certainly isn't a bad kit, but it tries to be two different things and as a survival kit it comes up a little short. This will serve well for a traveling family and in a pinch it will make a decent emergency kit, but I would not rely on it as a sole source.
text_fidelity_b: 94 Piece First Aid Kit Packed with First Aid and Survival Essential by Sirius Survival

Withings Pulse While I am only ten days into using my Withings Pulse Ox, I am very pleased with the purchase so far. Of all the devices currently on the market, this one seemed to offer the most bang for the buck. The step, activity, and sleep tracking seem to be quite accurate. The pulse and oxygen saturation monitoring are simple and precise. Battery life seems to be superb, and integration/connectivity with my iPhone have been no problem. Both the wristband and the belt clip are well-made and comfortable. I find that it really helps to motivate me to maintain and improve my health.

If I were to provide four pieces of constructive criticism they would be:
1) Make the Pulse OX waterproof or at least very water resistant.
2) Improve the Apple Healthkit Integration. I've had some issues, not in the Withings App, but within Healthkit, with doubling of steps.
3) Provide a means for background measurement of pulse and oxygen, rather than requiring the fingertip read. It is not practical to use for Zone Training or to see peak heart rate during a workout.
4) Allow for customization of the step and sleep goals.

Overall it has been a great little device though. Used in my "App Ecosystem" of the Withings App, WebMD, MapMyRun, and Healthkit...it is a nearly complete solution for my personal wellness goals.
text_fidelity_b: Withings Pulse

Double walled insulated tumblers are all that my husband and I use for drinks. I always like to have a drink with me and these type tumblers keep them nice and cold all day. My husband uses his for coffee that he takes to work with him every day, and I use mine for my diet Dr. Pepper. He uses his later in day for cold drinks after drinking hot drinks in the morning. The ability to take our drinks with us saves us a lot of money. We used to purchase drinks at drive through windows, or out of drink machines but since discovering what we call "cold cups" we just take our drinks with us. About this mug specifically, I love it. I have several of the name brand expensive tumblers, and this one keeps ice and keeps drinks hot just as well as those costing two or three or times as much. I love that this tumbler holds thirty ounces of drink. That is a lot of drink and since it stays ice cold when using ice with it, I can keep it with me at work for the better part of the day. The lid fits the tumbler perfectly. It has rubber ring to seal the lid tightly so that the cold or heat stays locked into the container. The lid has two holes in the top, one for drinking out of. I purchased stainless steel and hard plastic straws for my tumblers as, I prefer to drink out of a straw, but my husband drinks right out of the cup. However you decide to use it, the top stays smoothly on the tumbler and I haven't had problems with spills and leakage. Of course if you turn it completely upside down it will spill drink out, but using it normally, it doesn't leak at all. The bottom of the tumbler is crafted to fit perfectly in cup holders, making it easy to take on the go. I don't have to worry with rust or corrosion with this tumbler, since it is crafted of strong and durable stainless steel. When we are done using them, I just pop them in the top row of the dishwasher (lid and tumbler) and they come out perfect every time. I can keep ice in my cup overnight, so when I am watching TV on the bedside table, the cup is here with the lid protecting it from spills and keeping drinks ice cold. In the morning, I refill and the ice lasts throughout the day. I plan on purchasing several more for gifts for family members and co-workers and at just under 11.00 delivered to my door, they are affordable too! Since I never know what to buy for the men in the family, I think this would make a perfect gift for them too.

text_fidelity_a:
EASYANT Tactical Bushcraft Survival Kit 14 in 1 Tins for Camping Hiking Adventures Outdoor EDC Gear Kit Wow..!! You’re looking at a small sized all-inclusive survival kit that really packs a punch! For the sake of not being redundant and listing included items (see photo I used with the list!) This kit albeit tiny in stature, really holds those basic “urgent” items.. just like circus clowns fit in a toy car!! The overall footprint is perfectly small!! No bigger then, a standard 3x5 notecard- Which makes it a great option to easily tuck inside your gear bag, backpack, tackle box, car glovebox, prepper supplies, etc. Best part of all, when added to a bag- this is so light, you won’t even know it’s there! Mission accomplished.

Love the container- its reminiscent of an old fashion sardine can but, with a useable lid to keep it securely closed.. Fact- the container itself is a working piece to this kits overall function! Giving a lot of thought into keeping this minimal. Of course, being this small in size- you should expect this is just for emergent necessities. This couldn’t sustain a person more than a crisis and certainly wouldn’t suffice for multiple people needs. Items included come in increments of x1 (bandaids = x5) So, if traveling in a group for more then a day.. I’d suggest a larger kit or, at the very least supplement this one.. This has the ability to get you out of a tight spot and would say that’s it’s intended purpose!

Note: One thing I’d definitely recommend with this kit.. and can’t stress enough- is including a simple how too handbook or, guide sheet to take with Ha! Starting a fire with flint isn’t like flicking a switch! If emergent scenario.. it’s safe to assume, the situation is not ideal! So, if ever found in position to use.. it makes sense to have that helpful 411. It may be difference of life/death. (Wow.. I sounded like Dirty Harry just then- ha ha..!!)

If you are prepping for serious situations that could present in your circumstances.. One must also acquire a full first aid kit, food/water supply, Shelter- to subsidize an item like this. BUT, hopefully that is common sense if you’re truly thinking through being prepared!

A few simple adds to make this more complete: Safety pin, small bic lighter (bc, I saw in a post- fire is harder to start then, one might guess- oh, wait.. that was me!) I clipped onto this case a carabiner with a built-in flashlight!! Just those few little items can beef this up a bit. (would have loved to see them included with the set.)

Overall, this is made to avoid being caught empty-handed and could definitely step up to that task 100%. At this price point- this is a great gift for those who love to venture out into situations where they may find themselves needing to be prepared- this will do just that!! I hope this info can help in your decision.. feel free to let me know!
text_fidelity_b: EASYANT Tactical Bushcraft Survival Kit 14 in 1 Tins for Camping Hiking Adventures Outdoor EDC Gear Kit

text_fidelity_a: Portable Outdoor Shower, 2 Flow Mode, 4400mAh Battery Powered Shower Pump for Hiking/Backpacking, Travel, Beach, Pet, Flowering, IPX7 Waterproof &USB Rechargeable Camping Shower with 3 LED Lights… And I am happy to have it.  I am a "senior" and bought the senior parks pass that allows me to stay at a very small cost at many national parks as well as many state parks.  Sometimes I have found a place I want to camp that is more "rustic" than others - meaning no toilets or showers available.  I have a camping "porta-potty" and now I have this camping shower which is great!  What I added to this unit is a large bucket I got from the local grocery story - a large white bucket with a lid that I spray painted black.  That way, if I'm camping near a lake at a primitive campsite and go for a swim or hike around the lake, I will have the bucket sitting in the sun, full of water, and being black, it will warm the water up so it isn't just cold water I shower with when I come back from my swim or hike.  The size of the bucket works really well with this shower unit since the pump hangs higher on this bucket which seems to make the unit more stable.  The bucket itself is heavier with the amount of water I can add to it - I have a pair of "hydration bladders" which I fill before going out to the campsite, so using one of them for showering is fine for me.  I do think it's very odd that this usb charging unit has a plug that is not compatible with any other usb device you might have.  I mean, I have three types of usb plug that I use already and this adds number four to the mix.  Very strange...plus I have a few headsets that have a soft plug cover that can be difficult but this one is even more so - it's fragile, so I have taken great care not to accidentally snap it off.  When I go to primitive camping areas, I do have a larger "battery tender" that can charge my phone, laptop and this unit, but just in case, I have two small hand-size power packs and a solar charger just in case.  My tent is a good sized stand up tent with a front shade cover - for a shower area, I brought a couple of sheets and clothes pins so I can shower with a small amount of privacy - oh, and I have a fold up plastic bucket that is big enough for me to stand in so I can take much of the spent shower water and dump it away from the tent.  Yes, I may be camping primitive, but I do like having the civilized things like this shower unit with me.  Nice to feel clean after a sweaty hike!

Assembly was straightforward and without any issues. In use, it seems well made and sturdy. It's a typical flywheel design with a knob to adjust a resistance onto the wheel itself. The seat is completely adjustable for height and can be position more forward or rearward to further adjust your position relative to the pedals and the handlebars. The seat itself is nicely padded and reasonably comfortable, although I am considering replacing the seat with something wider. It uses a standard bicycle seat, so that should be an easy thing to do.

The pedals are those "steel trap" type with the jagged contacts that require you to wear shoes. I'm okay with that, but theres a nylon strap system that surrounds your toes. My size 12 feet means I'm pedaling on my toes. The pedals, therefore, were the first thing to be replaced. Again, it uses standard picycly parts so replacement was easy.

The control module is a simple battery operated counter. It can track miles, calories or time... or it can be set to cycle through the various measurements as you go. Theres no connection to the adjustable wheel resistance, so things like calorie burn are obviously just an approximation, at best. But that's pretty typical, I'm sure.

Overall, I recommend this bike. It seems well made and it gets the job done.

text_fidelity_a:
Kelley Coffey-Meyer's The Shape of Things to Come DVD (also called Complete Cardio Sculpting) This is the first DVD I've tried from instructor Kelly Coffey-Meyer, and I must say that I liked both the workout and Kelly very much. I found it very inspiring that Kelly, who has been involved in fitness for quite a long time, is a mom in her 40s, yet she seemingly had plenty of energy for this tough workout! This DVD contains a 50-minute circuit-style workout which alternates toning work with short cardio intervals. Some of the cardio work uses an optional step, but you could easily modify if you don't have a step (or substitute a small, sturdy stool, as you don't need much width). Kelly also uses two sets of dumbbells, which she labels "light" and "heavy"; I'm still trying to figure out what poundage is best for me, but for now, sticking to 5# the entire way through seems to work fairly well. The time breakdown listed on the DVD case is as follows: Warm-up, 4 minutes, Sculpting and Cardio, 34 minutes, Chest and Abs, 10 minutes, Stretch, 2 minutes.

The warm-up uses mostly basic, familiar moves, but somehow, Kelly makes them seem more fun! She includes knee-ups on the step and ends with some front and side kicks, which I loved. The first sculpting interval comes next and is focused on back/core. Using your "heavy" weights, you'll start with a very functional fitness-oriented "chop" move, first going halfway, then all the way down to the floor. Next comes a v-press, a front pull/press combo, and an underhand/overhand row, with the entire circuit repeated once. The first cardio interval begins with plyo lunges on the step (there is quite a bit of impact throughout the video, but again, it's easily modified), squat, slide, and step-knees. For the second sculpting segment, you'll focus on shoulders, this time using your "light" weights. Kelly begins with a unique side/front staggered raise, moves into a forward raise with upright row, and finishes with side delt raises and a shoulder press; again, the series is repeated. You'll then go back, repeat the previous cardio segment, and then repeat the entire shoulder work sequence once more.

The next cardio segment starts with jumping jacks--I usually hate these, but again, they were fun here! You do two jacks, a slow jack, and then a plyo X--a jump to each side while in a boxer's crouch--before finishing with hamstring curls on the step. The next sculpting interval consists of biceps work: hammer curls, side curls with a slow count down, half-up curls, and front elbow lifts; you then repeat both the jumping jack cardio series and the biceps work. The final cardio choreography has the most impact, and I found it to be the most intense as well. You'll do a wide jog, a skate from side to side, jump rope, and then plyo hops on the step. The last sculpting series works the triceps in several unique ways. First comes French presses and tricep kickbacks, but then you do a move which I've never seen before, sort of like an upright row behind your back, and you finish by lifting your arms straight behind you. The high impact-cardio and triceps work are both repeated.

Are you wondering when the leg work is going to come in? Well, the last standing segment is sort of a cardio sculpting series focused on the lower body. Using your heavy weights and moving very quickly, you'll squat and place both weights on the floor, squat and pick up one weight, squat and pick up the other weight, and then repeat the entire sequence MANY times (you may want to consider starting with lighter weights here). Next, you'll do what Kelly calls "a skater's lunge" but which I've usually seen called a curtsey dip: you'll lunge one leg behind the other on an angle, with the added twist of holding a dumbbell in your opposite hand and touching it to the floor in front of your static foot. You'll do all the reps on one side before moving to the other, then repeat the squat series (I was feeling pretty tired the second time through!), and finally, finish with the skater's lunge, alternating sides this time.

You're not done yet, though--now it's on the the floor for chest/abs work! Kelly lies on the step, but you can lie directly on the floor if needed. The chest series includes chest press, wide-angle chest press, 2-count chest flies, and lower chest/tricep pushes. The abs work was the only part of this video that I found a bit on the boring side, as it's just a simple series of crunches: crunch up, crunch lifting leg in and out, crunch lifting leg in/out and twisting to the side, and repeat on other side. Both the chest and the abs sequences are repeated once. Kelly finishes with quite a very quick stretch. Still lying on the step, she stretches the hamstrings, moves to seated for a chest/back stretch, stretches the neck on both sides, and yes, now you're done!

I really enjoyed this workout--the time flew by, particularly during the cardio intervals, and the toning work was fun, unique, varied, and had a functional fitness flavor (ie, mimicking movements from everyday life such as twisting). I would rate this as a high intermediate workout, but it would probably be doable for advanced beginners by using even lighter weights and going without the step (those wanting more of a challenge can heavy up on the weights if they dare and use a higher step). The DVD is very well-chaptered with various shorter workout options, such as just doing the cardio, completing only a single circuit, etc. Overall a great addition to my video library and highly recommended!
text_fidelity_b: Kelley Coffey-Meyer's The Shape of Things to Come DVD (also called Complete Cardio Sculpting)

Frankford Arsenal Quick-N-EZ 110V Case Tumbler Kit with Sifter for Brass Cartridge Cleaning and Polishing for Reloading [[VIDEOID:4d97ce6c49de579dc9b8d7678abf3b9f]] Maybe it is a little early for this review since I got this yesterday but I am very impressed and this has been run about 16 hours out of the last 20. I set it on a smart plug timer so it could even do a late night batch without running all night. I used to do ultrasonic cleaning but I hated the drying process and the less pleasing lack of that brassy shine you get with tumbling.
A couple pieces of advice....I saw reviewers mentioning the center bolt dinging up brass, the fix is SUPER easy. A simple drinking straw to cover the threads. I even found a blue one that matches the tumbler.
Second piece of advice, don't be dumb like me. I had a handful of .223 that I decided to add to the .40 cal I was tumbling. .223 fits in the .40 cal so many of the .223 had unpolished bases. Just remember 9 mm fits in .40 and .40 fits in .45. so pay attention if you mix brass. Make sure it can't fit inside the other type.

LEZYNE MTB Specific Micro Floor Drive Pump Read good reviews of the Lezyne Micro Floor Drive HV on [...] and figured I'd give it a try. My previous hand pump was too tiring on the arms when pumping up 2.2" tires on the trail. I needed a small floor pump version to carry with me in my CamelBak on my mountain bike rides. The pump I received weighed in at 210g. The mounting bracket was another 18g which I won't need. With my previous hand pump I could easily fit 2 fingers on each side of the T shaped handle for more grip. The Micro Floor Drive HV handle is quite small and I can only fit 1 finger on each side of the handle which feels awkward, but since I can now use 2 hands to press down it's not too bad. Overall I'm happy with this product, but wish it was a bit smaller in length and width.

+ Feels very solid

+ Can use like a floor pump

Cons:
- Longer and wider than a typical hand pump

- Somewhat heavy, weight 228g (210g pump + 18g mounting bracket)

I've been using this pump for almost 4 years now and have had zero problems pumping tires with Presta and Schrader valves. 100 pumps will get a 26 x 2.0 tire to a comfortable pressure (I estimate just below 30 psi). 120 pumps will yield a very firm tire. The foot peg makes pumping a breeze. I've updated the rating from 4 to 5 stars and added measurements below.

text_fidelity_a:
Alloy Car Roof Bike Bicycle Fork Mount Carrier Rack Max Load 44 lbs After reading the pros and cons of fork-mounting vs upright (wheel-mount) I decided to go with these, figuring the mostly aluminum structure would last a while and the fork-mounting would secure the bikes well. I've used the product one time on a short trip, but so far it seems sturdy and the bikes are locked on firmly. My one concern, which I knew in advance of purchase, is that the fork mount only holds the traditional thin skewers/axles. That works fine for our family fleet of tourers and hybrids from years 1998 through about 2012. However, a lot of new bikes now have the much fatter through-axles (particularly bikes w/ disc brakes). So if i get a new bike I'll probably need a new rack.

Vehicle: 2016 Subaru Outback

Pros:
-My big Cannondale Adventure 400 and my wife's Giant Sedona fit perfectly and are secured with front quick release and included rear hold-down strap.
-Reasonable price, though not as inexpensive as some all-steel models out there.
-No tools required, no customization needed for our Outback with factory folding roof rack.
-Seems and looks solid for those worried about appearance.

Cons:
-May need to fiddle with how many spacers to use with each bolt. There are six bolts on each rack.
-Installation, certainly the first time, might take up to 20 minutes for each rack. And sometimes it's hard to get those big wingnuts to thread properly given the awkward angle since the bolt is vertical and you may not have much space to install the wingnut between bolt and roof of car.
-Very easy to have the spacers fall off the bolts before wingnut is threaded. I had two or three roll off the back of our vehicle. No biggie on a flat concrete driveway but can be a problem on gravel or camping.
-It doesn't lock, which is okay for our needs. I can probably run a cable lock through the frame/tires and part of our roof rack. This may not keep the racks from being stolen but it would be a real pain to remove with bikes mounted. -Of course, it's nice to leave the rack on all summer if you use it frequently, but note someone can get a rack off in 3 minutes if there's no bike on it.
-For any roof rack, it may take a little strength and height to put the bike on top of a car/SUV and simultaneously align that front fork with the locking axle (built into the rack). I'm over 6 feet but my wife is 5'-6" - no way can she use this rack w/ her hybrid. Might be different w/ an ultra-light tourer and a foot stool.
text_fidelity_b: Alloy Car Roof Bike Bicycle Fork Mount Carrier Rack Max Load 44 lbs

text_fidelity_a:
EBAT LED Lantern Recharged by solar panel+USB Cable for Travel, Picnic, Hiking, Yellow [[VIDEOID:7cace53d54dd11d9ca86d52ec20f0527]] If you ever go camping or if you live in an area where there are frequent power outages you understand the need for a good lantern. I have worked with several lanterns and while I have used some that are a little brighter or a little more compact, this one is a decent one that has some good features. Besides having a couple of operation modes, it is chargeable via solar energy.

This is a reasonably bright lantern but it is not blindingly bright like some others I have seen. This is a trade-off in my book. If you are expecting something that is bright enough to light a small camp area and allow you to read by it, this is a decent lamp. If you want something to light a 20'x20' room it is not strong enough to provide color recognition through the whole room.

This lantern has a rechargeable battery that can be removed and plugged in to the provided power adapter for recharging. It can also be opened up to expose a pair of solar panels so it can be charged up via solar power. There is something very important to understand about solar charging, though – using the solar panels to charge this lantern takes a lot longer than if plugging the pack in. I have not tried to completely charge the lantern via solar power but in my experience solar charging takes roughly 4 to 5 times longer. That said, if you do not have the option to plug in, the solar panel is a superb option.

This lantern seems to be solidly made and resistant to easy breakage. So, I believe it would survive a drop from a short distance, though I would hesitate to test this theory. The hook loop on top is plastic but it seems sturdy enough to handle frequent use and abuse.

This lantern has two operation modes. It has two brightnesses – dim and bright. The dim light is enough to light a hallway when carrying this lantern though it is not going to work for tromping through the woods. The bright setting is not actually all that bright but it is enough to see through a large room and make out everything in it, though it does not cast enough light to see colors clearly at more than 10' or so.

Overall, this is a decent little lantern. It seems to be made well and it can be charged by either a power adapter or solar power. Just keep in mind that it is not going to charge quickly if using the solar cells to charge it up.

Disclaimer: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. Even though I received this product at no cost I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.
text_fidelity_b: EBAT LED Lantern Recharged by solar panel+USB Cable for Travel, Picnic, Hiking, Yellow

text_fidelity_a:
The Firm Zip Trainer Medicine Ball Kit I chose this workout system a bit blindly, but I'm glad I picked it to try out. Having recently been diagnosed as type-2 diabetic, I've been working on managing my condition by adding some daily physical activity and changing my eating habits. Just with walking 30 minutes a day has resulted in my losing about 20 pounds in the past three months (I want to lose 20 more). Now that I've lost weight, I find that I need to tone up. Being over 50, I wanted to do something that was easy to do and low-impact. This Firm Zip Trainer system is perfect for that.

Watching the videos for the first time I really didn't think this was much of a workout - but found trying the exercise that wasn't true. The series of movements that the instructors put you through really work and stretch your muscles. I think that is the thing I like most about these exercises, you get to use muscles that you probably don't use on a daily basis (especially if you're like me someone who sits at a computer for most of the day). I really feel my range of motion has improved since starting this program.

I've only been using this for about a month, and not every day at that. You need some room to do these exercise, and right now the largest clear space I can come up with is my unheated garage. And given it's winter, there's been a number of days when it was too cold to exercise out there.

With this kit, you get the large medicine ball - which can be zipped open to be used in a variety of ways. The medicine ball by itself is five pounds and when put the three pound core ball in it, it becomes eight pounds. That doesn't seem like a lot of weight, but when you're out of shape as I am you will get tired after just a couple repetitions. You also get three DVDs, two of which are the main exercise programs and a third which is a bonus video. You start with disc one, which walks you through the basics of the routines. There are four programs on disc one. Rev!, which is sort of introduction and runs for about 15 minutes, and three full length workouts (22 minutes each) - one for cardio, one to sculpt, and one that is and amped up routine. Each of the programs usually features three of the six instructors, with one leading the exercise and the other two in the background with one doing a modified starter version of the routine and the other doing a more advanced version. The instructor will explain the routine and do a quick demonstration before starting. It can be hard to follow along - so I would recommend watching the videos without doing them first, then go back and follow along. Also of note, the Zip ball doesn't get used in all the exercises - there are even some where they use regular weights (looks like they are using 10 pound dumbbells). They also use typical exercise mat for some things.

The exercise sets on the second DVDs are more of the same, but gives you more of a workout. The bonus DVD is a routine that works your feet (you do it bare foot) and your abs.

My guess is most people will watch the videos a couple times and then once they learn the routines quit playing them. I also think that people will cherry pick certain parts of the routines and create their own versions of the workouts (least that I what I will be doing). Like I mentioned before, I'm a bit over fifty and out of shape, so there is a limit to what I can do right now - as I improve I'll add in more.

Something to note - there are a couple booklets that come with this set. One of which has bios of the six trainers that are featured on the videos. These are some really fit women, and I assumed most of them were a lot younger that they apparently are. The youngest is 31 (or was when these were made), and the oldest is 43 (and most of them have had children). That really surprised me.

The other booklet that you get is a 48-page nutrition guide / meal planner. I mentioned I had already been losing weight and I've done that by going to a high-protein/low-carbohydrate diet (which is what my doctor recommended for my diabetes). This nutrition guide recommends that too. The booklet really doesn't provide any detailed recipes, but it does give you a pretty decent meal plan to follow (very similar to the one I was provided by my diabetes educator).

To wrap up this review I'll say that I'm enjoying this Zip Trainer kit, and I liked it enough that I went and bought the [[ASIN:B0056H4GHK The Firm Express DVD Kit]].

Something to maybe mention that might interest some people, these videos are a product of GAIAM, which is the company that also puts out most of the DVD sets for the Discovery Channel - shows like Mythbusters and Dirty Jobs.
text_fidelity_b: The Firm Zip Trainer Medicine Ball Kit

Leupold Tracer Performance Eyewear with Polarized Lenses I was recently doing a job out in the Yuma desert with the near 50-degree sun for two weeks. I found myself envious of a colleague who had sunglasses with very good coverage, as I realized mine were a bit weak for this evil sun. I then realized a lot of the sunglasses I always thought of as gaudy may have just been that large because they were also trying to achieve the safety-glasses standard. Well, these achieve that safety-glasses standard without being too over the top. They look good, but still relatively nondescript. They provide good coverage from the sun as well, but they are also not too dark so if you need to continue to wear them inside for the safety protection, you don't look like you're trying too hard to be cool. These are very nice to have in those many situations where you occasionally need safety protection, but don't want to be swapping out safety glasses with sunglasses and then not knowing where to put the one you aren't currently using.

All that, and they also seem very good quality and come with a great case. I will go out of my way to really take care of these, because I know lots of polycarbonates can scratch (finely) easily. Not sure if these have any scratch-resistant properties, but no use taking any chances! Nice glasses!

Hydracentials Insulated Stainless Steel Metal Water Bottle with Straw Lid - Vacuum Insulated Water Bottles, Keeps Hot and Cold - Sports Canteen Bottle This is the smaller version of the second generation bottle. More about that in a minute. The reasons why I love this are the smaller size that fits in the beverage holder in my vehicle, and the improvements that were made when the second generation was released.

Improvements include the double wall construction that not only keeps this one (and the [[ASIN:B00LFPS0CY Hydracentials Sporty 25 Oz]] sibling) from sweating, but provides the insulation to keep drinks colder longer.

I can attest that the eight hour claim is absolutely true. To be sure it does not keep it ice cold that long, but it sure keeps it cold. I left mine in my car - with the insulation sock that shipped with mine - and it was cold hours later. This was in 95 degree weather, which would have turned a regular bottle of water hot. I am serious about that/ I did not test this without the additional insulating sock, but I am guessing that the water would have not gotten any warmer than cool without it.

Mine also came with a pair of straw cleaning brushes. I have not used those yet because I have found that soaking the top, straw and bottle in hot, soapy water, rinsing with a jet of clear water and air drying work perfectly.

Do note that this is NOT for hot liquids. It was not designed for them, and a hot liquid would probably ruin both the straw and the swivel piece to which it connects.

For me this is the ideal size, but click on the link to the 25 ounce model if you like your water supersized. Either way I think you'll be happy with one of these models because they are an improvement over others on the market that I have used, including this brand's original bottle.
text_fidelity_b: Hydracentials Insulated Stainless Steel Metal Water Bottle with Straw Lid - Vacuum Insulated Water Bottles, Keeps Hot and Cold - Sports Canteen Bottle

text_fidelity_a:
YONEX Super GRAP 30-Pack Racket Grips In humid weather when I sweat a bit, I prefer the blue Tourna Grip overgrip or a leather grip roughed up with sandpaper. However, when it's dry and/or cold out, I find that those get a bit slippery so I go for something rubbery. I've tried similar Prince, Wilson, Babolat, and Tourna overgrips, but these Yonex Super Grap overgrips are my favorites. They're rubbery with good traction without being outright sticky. The color of the grip doesn't bleed onto the player's hand like some others do. They are reasonably durable, and over time turn kind of cloth-like where the rubbery outer layer has worn through. This is a fairly thin, non-cushioning overgrip (which I like).

A quick note on this pack: Finishing tape is included not as a roll, but as 30 pre-cut pieces bundled together with a rubber band. The finishing tape is a bit stiff, not as stretchy, and a little easier to break as others I've run across. So the finishing tape isn't the greatest, but it's perfectly serviceable. The overgrip tape itself is also pre-cut to length with an angled cut and adhesive strip on one end. The adhesive does leave some residue, but it can be cleaned off. I've not had any issues with the rest of the tape leaving any residue or being hard to remove from the grip.
text_fidelity_b: YONEX Super GRAP 30-Pack Racket Grips

text_fidelity_a:
DSMART V101 Fitness Tracker with Body Temperature Heart Rate Sleep Health Monitor IP68 Waterproof Pedometer Steps Calories Counter Smart Watch for Men Women Teens (Black) Let me start off by saying I've owned many of these cheap trackers, and this one isn't terrible at all. The color screen and the multiple faces is fun, but I hoped it would have more customization. I was really excited about the temp sensor, but I can't say it seems terribly accurate. Seems more like a gimmick. The step counter seems pretty accurate compared to other trackers including FitBit, Mi Band, a Michael Kors Wear OS and Samsung product I compared it to, and the battery life is pretty great as long as you don't have all the sensors running all the time (if you do constant heart rate monitoring, for example, expect to charge it every couple of days instead of weeks). I also like the way it charges, much like a similar product I've tried from Letscom. Rather than have a dedicated charger that might get lost in between uses, the charging port is behind the band! You remove one side, and plug the entire watch into a USB port to charge. I love this feature and have only seen in on a couple of other products. I wish more would adopt it instead of magnetic proprietary bases.
At the end of the day, if you just want basic step tracking, sleep tracking and phone notifications on a device that doesn't need to be charged so often, it's OK. Don't get it for the gimmicks like the HR monitor and temperature, I don't think those are accurate. But at the same time, there are more solid products like the Xiaomi Mi Band line which is made to a higher specification and very competitively priced to this one. It's nice having options, but make sure you compare your options before purchasing.
text_fidelity_b: DSMART V101 Fitness Tracker with Body Temperature Heart Rate Sleep Health Monitor IP68 Waterproof Pedometer Steps Calories Counter Smart Watch for Men Women Teens (Black)

I charged this item for several hours after receiving - there are not indicators that let you know when it is fully charged or still needing to be charged. I tried it as a hand warmer first.

The controls are very problematic - the enclosed instruction leaflet has text so small that it is impossible to read, even with a magnifying glass. The instructions on the Amazon Product Description page do not seem to accurately match this product, and attempting the required button presses/pauses do not seem to lead to a function you want. I kept turning the useless LED lights on when what I wanted was the warmer function.

When I was finally able to turn on the hand warmer function, I was very disappointed. There are 3 settings, which seem to be low, lower and very very low. The Amazon Product Description page indicates the highest setting should be 50 C - 55 C. This converts to 122 F - 131 F. This should be hot - very very hot. Instead, at the highest setting (called 3rd gear, curiously) the hand warmer is barely warm, not enough to even warm your hand effectively. The first 2 settings are even lower, and as equally useless.

I did not really need this as a power bank, but felt the need to test that function also. Besides the fact that there is no way to tell how much power is left in this device, or if it is charging or needs charging, it is very very slow to recharge my phone. I used a a 60W charging cable, and it took several hours to charge my phone from 47% to 95%. I gave up after that, frustrated at its slowness.

This device works poorly at either of its listed functions. Perhaps as a paperweight, but I don't think it would work well at that either. I unfortunately cannot recommend this product.

text_fidelity_a:
NODLAND Lightweight Backpack, 20L Foldable Ultralight Hiking Daypack Packable This backpack is a bit unexpected in its design. It folds into the interior pocket. Therefore, the pouch that it came in is actually the inside pocket of the central compartment. All I had to do was unzip the pouch and unfold the backpack from within that pouch. I then had to pull the pouch inside out so that it formed an interior zippered pocket and tuck the loop inside.

I think that the design is really neat. I was able to fit a couple of pounds of mandarins inside along with my wallet and a few other incidentals. I walked around with this a little bit and found it to be comfortable as long as I cinched the shoulder straps tighter. There is no padding in the straps, so walking more than one mile would most likely get uncomfortable. The material reminds me of the baggalini-type bags made of a strong nylon. However, this backpack is thin, so I do feel anything with sharp edges would tear through this after prolonged use. The material is water resistant. I actually put part of the pack under running water and the water just rolled right off.

There are two mesh water bottle pockets on each side and they fit my standard-sized water bottles just fine. There is also an exterior outside pocket. The tiny reflective strips at the edges of the outside pocket are a nice safety touch; however, the strips they put on the top interior of the water bottle pockets are useless unless those pockets remain empty. Someone did not think out that design.

Overall, for the current price of $15.99 plus 5% off with a coupon savings, I feel this is a very good deal. It packs small and light and is perfect to carry around for when an extra backpack is needed. This 20 (or 22L - depending on which part of the Amazon ad one reads) size is like a full-sized backpack without any cushioning. I would not put a laptop in here unless it is protected with a padded sleeve or otterbox type case.
text_fidelity_b: NODLAND Lightweight Backpack, 20L Foldable Ultralight Hiking Daypack Packable

Gaiam Sol Sticky-Grip Yoga Mat (5mm) This yoga mat has a lovely color and attractive patterns embossed in its textured surface. It is well made of high-quality, sustainable, latex-free rubber, and the ribbed bottom works well for preventing slippage on a smooth surface.

This mat out-gassed a slight chemical smell for a few days but it did eventually wear off.

The manufacturer claims this mat is "thick." It seems to me to be about the same thickness, or at best a tiny bit thicker, than the standard rubber mats provided at my gym. For what it is worth, I have this to say about all such mats: If your body doesn't come with it's own built-in "padding," it is a bruising experience to do yoga or calisthenic exercises on a hard floor while sitting or lying on this or any other thin, rubber mat. For that reason, there aren't any yoga mats of this type on the market, including this one, that seem "thick" to me personally. However, since that is a typical design feature among all rubber yoga mats, I am not grading down this mat for not being what I truly consider thick--a depth of three inches. That is the thickness of a different type of yoga mat, a [[ASIN:B003VQNM2I futon mat]], which I also own. The advantage of this mat over a futon mat is that it weighs 5 pounds vs 19 pounds for the futon mat, making it much more portable. It is also substantially easier to keep clean.

Speaking of cleaning this mat, it is not necessary to pay a lot of money for special yoga-mat cleaning solutions when a mat is made of rubber, as this one is. You can make your own quite inexpensively. Here are some examples:

1. Dilute white vinegar in a ratio of 1:16 (1 tablespoon per cup). Vinegar is a natural disinfectant. To increase disinfectant properties, you can add a tablespoon of fresh lemon juice or a few drops of any of the following essential oils which each have disinfectant properties: tea tree, eucalyptus, peppermint, lavender, oregano, lemon, and clove.

2. Dilute a biodegradeable liquid soap, such as [[ASIN:B00016QTYO Sal Suds]], in the same proportion as the white vinegar, 1:16.

3. You can add 1 tablespoon liquid soap to each cup of white-vinegar mixture to maximize cleaning effectiveness.

Instructions for use of cleaning solutions:

1. Put the cleaning solution of your choice in a spray bottle and shake well.

2. Spray the mat and use a clean rag or paper towel to scrub the mat.

3. If you use a soap mixture, you may want to go back over the mat with a clean, damp rag or damp paper towel in order to remove the soap residue. This is not necessary when you use a vinegar mixture.

Note that rubber is not harmed by water. This means that, if you wanted to, you could hose it off on your patio during warm-weather seasons and drape it over a patio chair or the rail of a deck or porch to dry.
text_fidelity_b: Gaiam Sol Sticky-Grip Yoga Mat (5mm)

text_fidelity_a:
ABUS Mini Ultra 410 Bike U-Lock I really like this lock. I have not had any of the defective shackle problems that some other reviewers are writing about; I hope that they were able to return the product for a replacement or refund. My shackle slides easily onto the U portion. It also slides on in either direction (the keyhole has to face down, but either end of the U slides easily into either hole). These mini-U-locks are great if you always lock your bike to a modern bike rack, which should be designed so the mini-U lock fits easily. The lock fits around the bike rack, my front wheel, and the frame, then you can use a cable or another lock around the rear wheel. The lock is too small to fit around a parking meter, but I never do that now that my city has bike racks all over the place. These mini-U locks are much lighter weight and easier to carry than the full-sized U-locks. This lock only comes with 2 keys so don't lose them (other brands include 3 or 5 keys with their locks). I would prefer a metal bike mount, but this plastic one hasn't failed on me yet. I do like the way the you lock the lock to the mount so it is very secure (no way for it to fall off when you are riding).

This lock has a Sold Secure silver rating, which is done by a well known independent European bike lock testing program. Some locks have a gold rating, but those are all much more expensive and much heavier than this one. A gold-rated lock is appropriate if you lock your bike for long periods of time on the street in a big city with a known bike theft problem (like San Francisco or New York City).

While this lock works great, I'm giving it only 4 stars because there are only 2 keys and also because the comparable OnGuard Bulldog mini-U-lock costs much less on Amazon (and comes with 5 keys).
text_fidelity_b: ABUS Mini Ultra 410 Bike U-Lock

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Charge 4 Special Edition Fitness and Activity Tracker with Built-in GPS, Heart Rate, Sleep & Swim Tracking, Black/Granite Reflective, One Size (S &L Bands Included) The fitbit as it comes out of the box (in late 2020) has lots of bugs. The settings function will lock it up if you try to use it. The weather app errors. It will not sync reliably. You would be thinking about returning it right now. But if you do some internet searches, you will find that these are known bugs that it leaves the factory with. If you install the mobile app, sync it and wait about 2 - 3 days the nyou will get the update that makes things work as they should. Do NOT uninstall the weather function of the fitbit just because it won't sync. If you do, it will no longer be available to re-install when device is updated. Just leave it there and wait for the update. Then weather and settings will work and syncing will become reliable.

It's absurd that fitbit would release such a defective product, but they do and they don't make any effort to tell you about the needed update.

After updating, it is quite a handy little tracker. The only fitbit tracker with a built in gps so you don't need to take your phone along. However be warned that your battery if fully charges will only last 4 - 5 hours when using the gps. It also takes a lot of time away from the standby time remaining.

Another feature they don't try to explain properly is the Spotify integration. Your fitbit can act as a very basic remote control for Spotify, but only if you subscribe to Spotify Premium. This means that to use the Spotify remote control feature you need 1) a paid Spotify subscription and 2) you need to have your phone with you. No music can be downloaded to the fitbit. It is just a simple play/stop/skip remote function for your phone and Spotify paid.

So those are all the things that fitbit doesn't want to tell you even after you buy it. After you get it updated, it is essentially a Charge 3 with built in battery sucking gps and paid Spotify remote control.

If you are new to fitbit and don't mind all the hassles getting it working right, it is a great little tracker. If you are thinking about upgrading from a fitbit Charge 3, the built in gps and Spotify remotes are the main differences.

Update: After all this it would never sync reliably. I would always have to reboot the device twice in a row to get sync started again. This hat do be done about every 36 hours.

Returned. Not worth it.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Charge 4 Special Edition Fitness and Activity Tracker with Built-in GPS, Heart Rate, Sleep & Swim Tracking, Black/Granite Reflective, One Size (S &L Bands Included)

Saver Pad Set I had an accident on my skateboard yesterday, hit my elbow pretty hard and quit for the day. I was going to wait for this protective gear before I started practicing Ollies or doing anything else risky, but my sore elbow was a good reminder to wait for the proper equipment to use before something like that (or worse) happened again.
This set of knee, elbow and wrist protectors is fairly well-made although light. The only thing I really don't like is the logo. After years in graphic-arts I have decided that I truly dislike high-visibility logos so I remove them by sanding or cutting them off. In the case of this "Triple-eight" with a horrible intersection of 3 eights the best method was flat black enamel paint that seems to have obliterated everything except the raised portions of the embroidery. Otherwise it's all black and low key. (This was my intent when I bought this kit and it worked well. Yay!)
The fit is fairly good for a mass-produced set of items, the big factor and the determination for S-M-L being the hand and wrist-guard, which I ordered Large. It's a little loose, but I have all sorts of foam sheets and leather pieces to custom-fit these important pieces, even to reinforcing the external portions as required. The knee and elbow pads are sort of a one-size-fits-all, but the same rules for modification apply.
Essentially, a very good buy for protection that is far better to have and not need than to really need and not have!
This is important stuff to wear, because a skateboard can become very dangerous suddenly without any warning. This kit, in conjunction with a decent helmet and good shoes (skate shoes) can make the difference in protecting those parts of your body that won't function very well unless they move freely without pain. Try being an artist or musician with a broken wrist. Try driving you car or riding your bike with a bad elbow or knee. It's in your best interest to protect yourself, because nobody else will, and if you still haven't figured it out getting hurt costs $$$!
text_fidelity_b: Saver Pad Set

text_fidelity_a:
Energizer TAC-R 700 LED Tactical Flashlight, Bright Rechargeable Flashlight for Emergencies and Camping Gear, Water Resistant EDC Flashlight, USB Cable Included, Pack of 1 I like this flashlight. It is made in China, but feels sturdier than the $10 generic non-rechargeable flashlights that I also see on Amazon. I trust the charging circuitry on an Energizer-branded flashlight more than on a generic flashlight (and the batteries in these flashlights are powerful enough that safe recharging is important). The flashlight has 3 brightness modes plus one flashing mode. I like that the strobe mode needs to be activated by a double-tap on the power button, so I am very unlikely to get that mode accidentally (and I hate flashlights that start strobing when I don't want them to). The steady mode has a nice wide uniform beam despite the flashlight having a compact size (1.2 inches at the widest). A lot of cheaper flashlights are bright only in the center, then fade rapidly towards the sides. I find the uniform beam to be much more useful.

Yes, the battery is not replaceable and the whole unit will have to be discarded when the battery no longer holds it charge. Hopefully that will be after hundreds of charges, which is many years for me and I'll probably lose the flashlight before that happens. If you use your flashlight for hours every day, then this may be a bigger concern to you.
text_fidelity_b: Energizer TAC-R 700 LED Tactical Flashlight, Bright Rechargeable Flashlight for Emergencies and Camping Gear, Water Resistant EDC Flashlight, USB Cable Included, Pack of 1

text_fidelity_a:
Kohree Portable Butane Gas Stove for Outdoor Cooking, 10,000BTU Camping Burner Stove with Dual Wind-Guard, Butane Single Gas Burner Backpacking with Carry Case for Travel, Hiking Trip, Home Emergency We have a small shed that we use in the winter to get away when snow has us limited, or in the other times of year to just get a fresh perspective on life. In the winter, we often will use our wood stove to get some water heated or make simple breakfasts. Having another little burner sounded like a good idea.

HOW WE INTEND TO USE THIS
We are using this in a shed on a stable table top. We are not taking this camping, so it will be in a protected area and not dragged around a lot.

STURDY?
For dragging this around- it is okay, but kind of flimsy. I would suggest a crate or box to protect it or wrap of some sort when camping and transporting.

CANISTER
I gave my husband specific instructions to get BUTANE canisters for this stove. He was doing the "I know, I am not stupid" routine despite me saying he HAD to be sure and he was annoyed at me for insinuating that he would ever not know the difference between anything in a hardware store.

He came home with Propane in canisters. Be sure to pay attention to the canisters you are buying. Do not get the refill canisters that you use to fill lighters with and do not get propane, even if it DOES look like a cheaper deal. *rolls eyes at husband*

WIND GUARD
The wind guard is flimsy. If you are planning to use this outside, it is not going to protect you terribly well from wind. It helps a little, but is not that stable.

PERFORMANCE
Once I got the right canisters we were able to take the stove for a run. It is a great little stove for a single pan meal or tea/coffee water. It heats quickly and as long as you don't have a huge heavy pan on it, it will stay well and be stable.

SURFACE
We have this on a solid table top. Plan on having a solid surface to stand this on as well. It is pretty lightweight, so you will want to guard against sliding and shifting around.

PORTABILITY
This is easy to transport, small enough to carry, and is not too heavy. It also tends to be not quite as sturdy as it could be.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is a nice little burner for emergencies. It works great in our shed, but outdoors, you need to be sure to have a stable surface that does not slide easily to put this on. It works well, but in wind, it might give you issues. Just be sure to get the right canisters before planning on using this.

MY RATING
FOUR STARS. I wish it was a little bit sturdier and did not slide around as much on the surface as it does. Otherwise it is a pretty decent little burner for emergencies and get-aways.
text_fidelity_b: Kohree Portable Butane Gas Stove for Outdoor Cooking, 10,000BTU Camping Burner Stove with Dual Wind-Guard, Butane Single Gas Burner Backpacking with Carry Case for Travel, Hiking Trip, Home Emergency
